verdict: Useful connections for testing; no demonstrated Schumann–ET contact link.
scope: This review distinguishes documentary assertions, measured geophysics, reported experiences, synthetic checks and missing causal or source-identification evidence. No new fundamental theorem, confirmed contact effect or new physical observation is claimed.

headlines.label: Sources
headlines.title: A corrected attribution
headlines.body: Official Bashar material does name frequency bands. That repairs a documentary overstatement; it does not validate those physiological or ionospheric assertions.

headlines.label: Methods
headlines.title: A failed test design retained
headlines.body: The first exact lag-adjusted toy could not reject at the chosen threshold. A separately versioned larger design resolves that specific resolution problem.

headlines.label: Interpretation
headlines.title: Association does not identify agency
headlines.body: Shared timing and ordinary leakage can reproduce observations attributed to a direct or exotic source. The missing discriminator is explicit in every claim card.

claims.title: Are recent Schumann “anomalies” evidence of contact?
claims.finding: The carried October23–29 station quick looks do not provide an admitted calibrated paired SR/contact series. The saved49complete Kp bins endOct29 03:00UTC and measure geomagnetic activity, not Schumann mode changes.
claims.missing: A calibrated, synchronized numeric baseline and predeclared anomaly metric; separate evidence for any claimed sender.

claims.title: Do occult or channeling sources actually mention frequencies?
claims.finding: Gateway contains a proposed body/ionosphere mechanism. The official Bashar handout lists theta3–8Hz; an authorized transcript attributes40–100cycles/s gamma language. This corrects the older blanket “no Hz” attribution.
claims.missing: Document attribution does not supply measured transfer, dose, physiological response or verified communication.

claims.title: Does shared EEG/Schumann frequency prove coupling?
claims.finding: The inspected2026 spectral paper explicitly lacks simultaneous magnetometer records. Wang2019 tested rotations of roughly35µT fields, a different stimulus from illustrative1pT oscillations.
claims.missing: Concurrent calibrated channels, artifacts and matched controls; a specified coupling mechanism.

claims.title: Do similar messages identify a common ET source?
claims.finding: The2026 prospective study uses three channelers and28topic prompts. Semantic organization is an empirical text-analysis result, but origin remains unverified. Its companion qualitative paper shares the dataset.
claims.missing: Concealed unpredictable information, leakage audit, objective locked scoring, replication and additional source-discriminating evidence.

claims.title: Can astrology or Hermetic correspondences improve the test?
claims.status: Candidate timing controls or cultural interpretation
claims.finding: UTC, local solar time and astronomical geometry can be frozen nuisance variables. Symbolic classifications are interpretations unless they improve a predeclared held-out prediction against a matched calendar baseline.
claims.missing: Authenticated original event times, fixed features and external evaluation; relabeling one calendar is not independent evidence.

claims.title: Does a government archive validate the claimed mechanism?
claims.finding: The1983 Gateway document is an assessment. The1995 AIR evaluation distinguishes disputed laboratory interpretation from operational reliability. Archival custody does not identify extraterrestrial agency.
claims.missing: Inspectable experiments that discriminate the proposed explanation from ordinary alternatives.

claims.title: Is the new holographic framework already demonstrated?
claims.finding: The inspected Cavaglià–Tuszynski paper proposes neural/Schumann connections and states no data were used. It can suggest a model contract, not certify an effect.
claims.missing: Dimensioned coupling parameters and independently measured predictions; full theory audit is outstanding.

edges.reason: Revelatory narratives are a comparative cultural motif; similarity does not authenticate a modern external communicator.
The report proposes a body/ionosphere interpretation; the selected passage is not a calibrated coupling experiment.
The official handout supplies an attributed EEG-band/ionosphere assertion; it does not establish a Schumann-to-brain coupling.
Faraday arithmetic tests the stipulated uniform-field receiver model; no current station measurement is inferred.
Reported responses to geomagnetic-strength directional rotations cannot be transferred to picotesla Schumann oscillations without a new test.
Concurrent calibrated neural and geophysical records are absent from the inspected spectral correspondence study.
Sentence similarity measures discourse organization; it does not measure access to hidden unpredictable targets.
Bashar corpus methods and the three-channeler study offer related attribution problems; they are not the same sample or independent source authentication.
Astronomical timing can define nuisance covariates; symbolic zodiac labels require separate held-out evaluation.
Exact shared-driver and direct-model predictions coincide until independent variation is assumed.
A fixed concealed-target endpoint can test a specified chance model, conditional on independent assignments and leakage controls.
Even above-chance information would not distinguish extraterrestrial agency from matched ordinary leakage or other alternatives.
The prior same-port witness model leaves an ordinary source observationally equivalent to an exotic label.
A declared measurement channel supplies one acquisition requirement, not authentication of calibration or event times.
Locked timestamps, lag families and eligible non-events are necessary for the intended association analysis.
A synchronized packet and controls are prerequisites; metadata readiness alone never establishes a biological mechanism.
Identifiability within a two-column linear model does not authenticate a communicator or an extraterrestrial cause.

rounds.title: Sources, repository pins and the novelty gate
rounds.question: Which occult, Schumann and contact links have actually been documented or measured?
rounds.result: Selected current public repository files and primary studies were inspected. Official Bashar material does name frequency bands; the earlier blanket no-Hz attribution was corrected. No admitted synchronized Schumann/contact dataset or authenticated ET source was found in the inspected material.
rounds.critique: Recent text-similarity, EEG-spectrum and SR/physiology papers already cover nearby ideas. Proceed as evidence and methods engineering; the next test must specify a physical input and receiver.

rounds.title: Dimensioned electromagnetic acquisition
rounds.question: What can the stated magnetic signal induce in a specified ideal coil?
rounds.result: The illustrative 1 pT RMS, 7.83 Hz field gives 49.1973 nV RMS for 1,000 turns of 1 m². Producer 65 assertions and 151 independent comparisons passed, including zero-sensitivity cases.
rounds.critique: A stipulated coil and resistor-only noise model are not a feasible detector, tissue dose, biological response or sender identifier. Next, test timing and lag-selection artifacts.

rounds.title: Lag selection exposes a powerless toy
rounds.question: Does correcting for searched lags control a known finite randomization null?
rounds.result: One 32-offset fixture gave 7/32 rejections for the invalid selected-lag test. The adjusted test gave none. Independent review proved its minimum possible adjusted p was 7/32, so it could never reject at 0.05. The distinct-shape null fixture and all-lag p = 1 control were retained.
rounds.critique: Correct calibration alone is not useful sensitivity. Preserve the failure and predeclare a larger group; real calendar dependence still needs its own justified null.

benchmark.label: Round 3 / preserved limitation
benchmark.title: A correct test can be unable to detect anything.
benchmark.result: Seven searched lags across 32 cyclic offsets force corrected p ≥ 7/32. At α = 0.05 this design cannot reject for any input. The invalid selected-lag test nevertheless rejected 7/32 offsets in one fixture.
benchmark.limit: Zero adjusted rejections are not evidence that an effect is absent. This is a synthetic finite-group demonstration, not an empirical anomaly detector.

rounds.title: Resolve test granularity; expose a common cause
rounds.question: Can a larger finite test detect alignment, and does alignment identify a mechanism?
rounds.result: The separately versioned 256-offset design permits an aligned p = 7/256. Both producer fixtures retain 7/256 adjusted null rejections, with naive counts 77/256 and 75/256. In the shared-driver example, observational rank is 1 with nullity 1; only a stipulated independent perturbation gives rank 2.
rounds.critique: The sensitivity example is not a population-power estimate. More sensors or calendar labels do not establish the independent-intervention premise. Next, separate information accuracy from agency.

benchmark.label: Round 4 / two distinct limits
benchmark.title: Better statistical resolution does not identify the cause.
benchmark.result: With 256 offsets, the aligned example reaches p = 7/256 = 0.02734375. Yet X = z, Y = 2z fits both Y = 2X and a shared-driver model. Their observational design has kernel (1, −1). A hypothetical independent perturbation produces rank 2 and Gram determinant 28.
benchmark.limit: The cyclic null and hypothetical intervention are assumptions. These calculations do not validate them for actual field recordings or channeling reports.

rounds.title: Hidden information, leakage and numerical repair
rounds.question: What would a fixed concealed-target score establish, and how does leakage change it?
rounds.result: For 100 actual four-choice guesses under the declared null, the 5% rejection threshold is 33 hits. An ordinary independent leak with probability 0.2 gives the same q = 0.4 hit-count law as any stipulated independent mechanism with q = 0.4. A positive-tail underflow defect was reproduced, archived and repaired before acceptance.
rounds.critique: At 40 hits and 10 compromised trials, the preselected-subset tail is 0.0472839, while the arbitrary-after-outcome corruption bound is 0.149541. Actual leakage is unknown. Next, require custody, chronology and data provenance without pretending metadata authenticates them.

benchmark.label: Round 5 / fixed-trial arithmetic
benchmark.title: A score cannot name its information source.
benchmark.result: For 40/100 four-choice guesses, the specified no-information tail is 0.000686592. With m = 10 assumed compromised trials, the preselected-subset model gives 0.0472839 and the arbitrary-outcome-corruption bound gives 0.149541. A 20% perfect-leak mixture has q = 0.4 and the same count distribution as another independent source with q = 0.4.
benchmark.limit: There were no human trials. The actual leakage count is unknown. Exact binomial scoring assumes a guess on every trial; pre-reveal abstentions retained as nonhits require the conservative-reference distinction in the protocol. No ET probability follows.

rounds.title: Adversarial evidence intake and a prospective protocol
rounds.question: Can a complete-looking packet incorrectly become authenticated contact evidence?
rounds.result: The staged validator separates documentary, environmental, information and paired metadata readiness. A fully fabricated packet can satisfy structural requirements but always remains unauthenticated. Actual quick-look/Kp/corpus availability descriptors do not become paired evidence. One published target digest was matched by hashing four candidate strings.
rounds.critique: Hashes identify checked bytes, not truthful timestamps or secrecy. Declared nonce length does not prove entropy. A ready packet still requires independent calibration and custody review. Stop after these six rounds; acquire discriminating evidence before another discovery cycle.

benchmark.label: Round 6 / metadata is not authentication
benchmark.title: Keep an attractive packet from certifying itself.
benchmark.result: Malformed units, dates, Nyquist settings, reveal chronology, trial counts and unpaired intervals are challenged independently. Complete fabricated observational metadata can be structurally ready while evidenceAuthenticated remains false. The four-target unsalted-hash demonstration recovers the selected target by enumeration.
benchmark.limit: This is not a cryptographic break or proof that a salted scheme is secure. The code does not fetch or authenticate referenced data, calibrations, randomness, custody or subjective reports.

protocolSteps: Define the question and unit: field anomaly, physiological response, information accuracy, or sender identity. Do not substitute one endpoint for another.
Freeze the actual original event time in UTC, clock uncertainty, location, inclusion rules, every eligible session and all misses. Upload and repost dates are not substitutes.

Specify Bx/By or Ez units, sample rate, anti-aliasing, calibrated complex response, noise, station QC, checksum-bound data and matched baseline. A colored screenshot is not a calibrated numeric series.
For hidden information, separate target custodian, participant, scorer and analyst. Lock responses before reveal, retain all trials and audit independent target generation and concealment.

Do not expose a small target through an unsalted hash. Independently audit unpredictable secret nonces, commitment custody and disclosure chronology; a nonceBits declaration does not prove entropy or secrecy.
Predeclare the estimator, lag family, null transformations, nuisance/calendar variables, stopping rule, uncertainty and held-out replication. Check resolution and power before acquisition.
Keep information accuracy and environmental association as separate hypotheses. Audit shared drivers, leakage, missingness and ordinary receiver artifacts before interpreting either.
Treat a schema pass as metadata readiness only. Verify referenced raw bytes and independent audit records; never auto-promote a ready packet into coupling, contact or ET evidence.

roadmap.task: Acquire one bounded calibrated environmental packet and its response/noise/QC records.
roadmap.gate: Document license, original time base and a matched numeric baseline; otherwise keep recent anomaly unresolved.

roadmap.task: Specify a concealed-target protocol with independent custody and a defensible leakage bound.
roadmap.gate: Prospective consent/ethics and actual custody procedures before human data collection; no sessions executed here.

roadmap.task: Evaluate fixed calendar/astronomy covariates against a time-only baseline.
roadmap.gate: Authenticated original sessions and untouched held-out data; no post-hoc zodiac/lag search.

roadmap.task: Reproduce the closest2026 SR/EEG or text-analysis result if its data and methods become auditable.
roadmap.gate: Label replication; preserve same-dataset dependence and report exact data/control limits.

roadmap.task: Admit a new coupling or novel theorem question only after the prior-art gate.
roadmap.gate: Exact residual gap, dimensioned model, matched baseline and falsifier. Another automatic debate cycle is not evidence.
